text: Darsheel Safary, born on 9 March 1997, is an Indian actor known for his work in Hindi and Gujarati films and television. He made his film debut in 2007 with the critically acclaimed drama Taare Zameen Par, directed by Aamir Khan, where he played the leading role of Ishaan Nandkishore Awasthi, a dyslexic student. Safary was discovered by script writer and creative director Amol Gupte in late 2006 while searching for a male lead; after reviewing hundreds of auditions, Gupte selected him from Shiamak Davar's dancing school, "Summer Funk," during a scene where boys were asked to describe how they would "bunk" school. Gupte recalled, "It was a tough call. But Darsheel has the mischief in his eyes to be Ishaan. Everyone just naturally gravitated towards him." His performance was widely praised by critics, with Taran Adarsh of indiaFM calling him a "Master" and stating his performance deserved a special award, while Rajeev Masand of CNN-IBN described Safary as a revelation, saying he "steals your heart" and "carries this film completely on his shoulders." Other reviewers hailed him as the "real star of the film" and noted his performance as "brilliant." In a 2007 interview, Safary mentioned that his career aspirations included singing, dancing, or becoming a businessman or jewellery designer. His second film, Bumm Bumm Bole, released in 2010, reportedly earned him ₹3 lakh, the highest amount paid to any child actor at the time. He also starred in Disney India's superhero film Zokkomon (2011) and Deepa Mehta's Midnight's Children (2012). In 2012, he participated in the dance reality show Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa with Avneet Kaur, finishing in seventh position. He took a break from acting to focus on his studies. In 2016, he appeared as Abhay in the anthology series Yeh Hai Aashiqui. In 2023, he featured in the Hindi sports drama film Hukus Bukus and the Gujarati film Kutch Express.
